en: Saines showed you a large wooden crate packed full of medicine.{w}
note: Recipient of 'showed' unstated; 'you' (the party), since the next line says the gift is for the player (anata).

en: "This is... from that old lady at the apothecary?"{w}
"She says it is a token of her gratitude to you, for rescuing her son Almite."{w}{p}"However, it is more than this temple alone could ever use up... What shall we do?"{w}
note: musuko = son: Almite (glossary gender 'unknown') is male. 'She' = the old lady (obaachan).

en: "In that case, why don't we leave it with the Kernel Shop?{w}Their selection's always been poor anyway, and they don't even stock medicine properly. It's a good opportunity."{w}
"I see. Let us do that."{w}

note: List kept on separate lines. Item names are provisional (not in glossary; ITEM.CSV en empty): zenkai no kusuri, mahikeshi-gusuri, yotsuyu no nodoame. Align with the item table once it is translated.
Provisional item names (not in glossary): chinshin herb (cures confusion), hatsukoibana no kessho (cures charm), kaisekisui (cures petrification). Align with the item table.

en: "Oh? Is this your first visit? I am Saines, the bishop here."{w}

"Welcome to the Temple of Orses. What Orses governs is the power of life."{w}{p}"Within a life that may be called but a fleeting instant, we all strive to leave something behind, however small.{w}That is a precious and a lovely thing to do."{w}{p}"I ask that you, too, burn that life of yours for someone, for something."{w}{p}"Love directed at another will surely come back to you many times over."{w}
note: Orses' gender unknown: name repeated, no pronoun.

en: "One of our duties is to show souls the right path, from life's creation to its dark oblivion."{w}{p}"Life is born, grows, and dies.{w}It is a single path, and the souls that walk it to the end are led to the god of Dark Oblivion."{w}
note: somei kara anmetsu made: the two glossary title words used as process nouns (creation / dark oblivion). anmetsushin = glossary 'god of Dark Oblivion'. | Editorial: 'That exists as a single path' was stilted translationese; 'It is a single path' keeps the meaning.

en: "At times, however, some stray from that path and become beings of the in-between, wandering between this world and the other side."{w}{p}"Souls of the in-between that roam on even in death -- that is, evil spirits and the undead -- are said to be beings that have strayed from the law of life laid down by the god of Dark Oblivion."{w}{p}"The act of guiding them onto their proper path is what you all know as Dispel."{w}
note: hazama no tamashii = glossary 'souls of the in-between'; hazama no sonzai -> 'beings of the in-between' to match.

en: "Dispel is not a means of attack. It is an act of compassion that guides the souls of the in-between onto the holy path.{w}I ask that you never forget that."{w}
"Exactly. Dispel is an act overflowing with love."{w}
"Ah, Sigret."{w}
"Rest assured.{w}Should your souls ever stray from the path, I will take you by the hand and guide you every step of the way."{w}
"And then, through the act of love called Dispel, I will take your souls and once more...{w}
note: Opening fragment repeated inside {0E}/{0F} in SCDWMAP:3294; keep the two wordings identical. Ends on 'once more...' so the punchline in 3294 lands.

en: {0E}"And then, through the act of love called Dispel, I will take your souls and once more...{0F}kill the hell out of them."{w}
note: bukkorosu: crude, violent 'kill' (Saines next scolds her for the language). Rendered 'fucking kill them' to keep the coarseness; 'once more' = kill the already-dead souls a second time. Softer fallback if the project prefers: 'kill them dead'. | ACC: bukkorosu is coarse slang but not a taboo swear word (common in all-ages manga); 'fucking' overshot it by a notch. 'kill the hell out of them' keeps the crude register and still earns Saines' 'such language' scolding. 3292 build-up unchanged and still matches.

en: "As I keep telling you.{w}A sister must not use such language..."{w}
note: Desukara (sentence-initial, exasperated) = 'as I keep telling you'.

en: "Good luck with your adventures. Ufufufu."{w}
Sigret left.{w}
"Honestly... Please do not think ill of her.{w}In her own way, she worries about all of you."{w}
"Hello, everyone. You look well."{w}{p}"I am sorry to cut our greetings short, but I have patients to treat, so if you will excuse me for a moment."{w}{p}"If you need anything, please ask Sigret."{w}
After Saines left, you looked toward the temple altar and saw Sigret offering a prayer to Orses.{w}
note: Subject of miru (looked) restored as 'you' (the party).

en: What could she be praying for, and for whom?{w}Even from behind, you could sense how sincere Sigret's feelings were.{w}{p}Before you knew it, the bustle of the town had faded into the distance, and time was passing quietly...{w}
note: dare no nani o negatte iru = 'what, and for whom'. sono senaka kara ... tsutawatte kuru = her sincerity comes across from her back. | Editorial: tense aligned with the past-tense narration in the same row ('Before you knew it ... had faded') and in 3304/3308.

en: After a while, Saines came back.{w}

"Do you know what she is praying for?"{w}{p}"It may surprise you, but... Sigret is praying for the spirits of the dead."{w}{p}"When she was still young, I taught her about the path of souls."{w}{p}"When Sigret learned that souls of the in-between existed, she was terribly angry, and terribly sad.{w}'How pitiful,' she said."{w}{p}"To that girl, even the spirits of the dead -- your enemies -- are someone to be saved."{w}{p}"In fact, she even goes around saying that it is the spirits of the dead, above all, who truly must be saved."{w}
note: shiryo = 'spirits of the dead' (no glossary entry). ano ko = 'that girl' (Sigret is female). | Editorial: clumsy inverted word order ('are to that girl someone') reordered; meaning unchanged.

en: "...It is just that her feelings run so deep, she blurts out the strangest things, which is really rather..."{w}
note: Trailing nan to mo... kept unfinished.

en: Having finished her prayer, Sigret stood up.{w}
"Oh, Bishop Saines. Are you done with the treatments?"{w}
note: Saines-sama from Sigret -> 'Bishop Saines' (his settled title) here and in 3341.

en: "Yes. You retrieved them so quickly that everything went smoothly."{w}
note: anata no kaishu = Sigret's retrieval of the wiped-out party; 'them' = the patients.

en: "Thank goodness... Well then, I have the next retrieval request to... Excuse me."{w}
Sigret gave a little bow and hurried off.{w}
"Please take care, all of you, as well..."{w}
"I hear Semnadoc is a town brimming with faith.{w}Apparently Archbishop Mersenne, who reached that rank so young, is most zealous."{w}{p}"We must learn from their example."{w}
note: Mersenne-dono, wakakushite daishikyo -> 'Archbishop Mersenne'. minarawanakereba has no object; 'their example' covers the town and Mersenne. | Editorial: 'quite the zealous one' was flippant against the honorific source and Saines' formal voice.

en: "I should not have told her after all..."{w}{p}"There is a bizarre thing called the Gate of the Underworld...{w}It is said that when its door is opened, a great many spirits appear.{w}Most likely they are magical creatures born of some evil will."{w}{p}"A rumor reached us that a ritual to open the Gate of the Underworld is being performed beneath the Madrie Church Cemetery."{w}{p}"I heard it from an adventurer myself, but Sigret pressed me for the details.{w}I thought I knew that girl..."{w}
note: Source typo semararete shimaimaite read as shimaimashite. Saines is evidently explaining Sigret's departure to the party. | Editorial: per lead decision, pages 1-3 copied verbatim from slice_011 SCDWMAP:3203 (same Japanese; mahou seibutsu = the spirits, 'they are magical creatures'; 'told her'). Last page kept (its Japanese differs: ano ko no koto vs seikaku).

en: "Sigret..."{w}

"We clergy uphold the teachings of the gods, but we also have the bad habit of leaving everything in the gods' hands."{w}{p}"Among us, Sigret is a rare sister, one who studies the gods' teachings while thinking and acting for herself."{w}{p}"Her conduct and attitude being... what they are, her reputation at other temples is not very good, but I am proud of her."{w}
note: kami read as plural 'the gods' (polytheist setting). are (euphemism) -> '... what they are'.

en: "Welcome back, Sigret.{w}Are you keeping well?"{w}
"Yes. And I see you are as well as ever, Bishop Saines."{w}
"There is little I can do, but I am praying that you and your friends travel safely."{w}
You offered a prayer to Orses, god of life-creation.{w}
note: Somei-shin = glossary 'god of life-creation'. The gap after the name in the source is kept out (likely a fixed-width name field).

en: Please guide us, children of the gods, the spirits and the land...{w}
"You wish to perform the Rite of Flux?"{w}{p}"......{w}I was told by my predecessor that this rite is not to be performed lightly."{w}{p}"If you truly insist, I will perform it, but......"{w}
The Rite of Flux randomly redistributes the divine relics and other items you have not yet obtained.{w}{p}The current state cannot be restored afterwards, so please be careful.{w}
Perform the Rite of Flux?
"Just to be sure, I must ask..."{w}
"You truly want the Rite of Flux?"
note: Choice prompt, 34 chars incl. quotes (source 19 full-width chars); shortened from 'You truly wish to perform the Rite of Flux?'. Check fit. | Editorial: pro-drop rule: subject and finite verb restored in Saines' quoted question; same length (34 chars), in-game fit check still open.

en: "Very well.{w}As the fee, I must ask for an offering of 100,000 GP."{w}
note: Source G.P. -> 'GP' per convention.

en: Will you pay?
"Then let us perform the rite."{w}
The divine relics you had not yet obtained scattered once again across the world.{w}
"May this rite bring light to the road ahead of you all..."{w}
"Everyone, it seems your offering is... not quite enough."{w}
"I see. That may well be a wise decision.{w}Trials are not something to avoid, but something to face."{w}{p}"May the blessing of Orses be upon you all..."{w}
"Then I cannot perform the rite..."{w}
Who will pay?

note: op0fb label row (likely debug/status text); 'sentaku shita hito' = person chosen.
torihiki seiko = transaction succeeded.

en: * Deal failed: {0B:0003:0000}
note: torihiki shippai = transaction failed.

en: You don't have enough money.{w}
"What...? Lady Urna has been restored...!?{w}Ahh...!!{w}Thank goodness... Truly, thank goodness..."{w}
note: saisei sareta -> 'restored' (regenerated); 'reborn' is the alternative. | ACC: Urna-sama -> 'Lady Urna' per lead convention (review_notes: 'Lady Urna ... stay'; glossary term 'Lady Urna'; 31 other corpus rows use it). Ragnastia is Urna's child and reveres her.

en: The queen, who is both a priestess of Fiona and a child of Urna, quietly closed her eyes and offered a prayer.{w}
note: shinkan -> 'priestess' (glossary position: priestess of Fiona; Ragnastia is female).

en: "When I heard a little while ago that the Four Sages had been making big moves here in town, in Semnadoc and elsewhere, I wondered if perhaps..."{w}{p}"Did Lady Urna seem well?{w}I see... A new land, with Raizam and the others..."{w}{p}"I have the deepest respect for Princess Leafa of Isfald."{w}{p}"To think she could issue a royal command relying on nothing but faint memories.{w}So the blood of the elven royal family has flowed on unbroken after all."{w}{p}"And the ogres and goblins, too, kept faithfully guarding the promised item all this time...{w}Nn... uuh..."{w}
note: jokamachi = the town below the castle ('here in town'). chokumei -> 'royal command' (kept distinct from the Decree). Raizam-sama -> 'Raizam' (gender unknown). yakusoku no shina read as one item (the wine); could be plural. | ACC: Urna-sama -> 'Lady Urna' per lead convention (review_notes: 'Lady Urna ... stay'; glossary term 'Lady Urna'; 31 other corpus rows use it). Ragnastia is Urna's child and reveres her. | Editorial: 'bow my head to' was a literal calque of atama ga sagaru (deep respect/admiration), which reads oddly in English.

en: Perhaps the feelings she had held back were finally pouring out.{w}Tears were welling up in Ragnastia's eyes.{w}
"I've felt so alone all this time...{w}Because I was the only one who knew the truth behind this great upheaval..."{w}
"But everyone remembered, didn't they!{w}In different ways, but all of them were thinking of Lady Urna..."{w}
note: ACC: Urna-sama -> 'Lady Urna' per lead convention (review_notes: 'Lady Urna ... stay'; glossary term 'Lady Urna'; 31 other corpus rows use it). Ragnastia is Urna's child and reveres her.

en: "Thanks to you delivering the wine, my heart has been saved as well.{w}I don't know how to thank you enough..."{w}{p}"Oh, I know. Please take this.{w}As a token of my gratitude."{w}
note: budoshu = the wine (the Yuan Wine of the ogres, per glossary note).

en: "I think I'll try sending letters to Princess Leafa and King Montana."{w}
"To thank them, and to say I hope we'll keep getting along from here on."{w}
Ragnastia gave a warm smile.{w}

"How do you do. I am Queen Ragnastia, ruler of this city of Bistel."{w}{p}"Thank you very much for taking an interest in the Decree."{w}{p}"Ideally, I would have you search for the eight divine relics right away, but we have only a limited number of the tools needed to find them."{w}{p}"So, though it is rather rude of me, we have prepared a test, and we give the tools only to those who pass it."{w}{p}"The site of the trial is Loipes Cave. Hidden in this cave is an object called the Jewel Ring."{w}{p}"If you can bring the Jewel Ring back from the cave, you pass the test."{w}{p}"Please take this compass."{w}
You received the Jewel Ring compass.{w}
note: jueru ringu no konpasu: compass tuned to the Jewel Ring; 'compass' lowercase per glossary.

en: "This is a replica of the compass used to search for the eight divine relics, made so that it reacts to the Jewel Ring."{w}{p}"The real search for the eight divine relics uses a compass too. You might call this a rehearsal for the relic hunt."{w}{p}"Now, the compass cannot be used as it is. To make it work, you need something called Fame."{w}{p}"Fame is something only those recognized by the gods can obtain.{w}For now, I will lend you four of my Fame."{w}
note: Fame counted as a unit ('four of my Fame', 'three or more Fame') as the source does (yottsu).

en: Ragnastia lent you four Fame.{w}

"Once you enter Loipes Cave, stay calm and steady, and set up camp."{w}{p}"Once you have made camp, offer Fame to the compass I just gave you."{w}{p}"If you put in three or more Fame, the compass will show you with light where the object you seek lies, so try following it."{w}{p}"When you come near the Jewel Ring, the compass will show you its location with light."{w}
note: awatezu sawagazu = without panic or fuss -> 'stay calm and steady'.

en: "Well then, I look forward to good results.{w}Do your best... Hm?"{w}

"Everyone, this may be an odd question, but... do you have an Angel's Window?"{w}{p}"Um, this item here."{w}{p}"With one of these, the surrounding terrain is always displayed, so it's handy for not getting lost..."{w}
"Oh, is that so. You don't have one...{w}Hmm, what to do.{w}...Ah, I know."{w}
"Someone. Is anyone there?"{w}
Soldier
